_what_this_is: The entry gate, answered BEFORE drafting. The threshold question is whether a well-informed non-expert would confidently believe something the primary sources do not support.

belief._note: What the reader already believes, stated as they would state it. If you cannot write this sentence, there is nothing to correct and no subject -- which is how the tobacco-analogy candidate died.
belief.statement: Removing CO2 from the air can't replace cutting emissions. Today almost all removal comes from trees and forests, and machines like direct air capture remove a trivial amount at high cost. To reach net zero we'll still need a lot more removal later this century to cancel out leftover emissions from things like aviation, farming and cement, but it's risky to count on technologies that don't exist at scale yet.
belief.how_we_know_they_believe_it: The coverage that settled it. Named outlets, quoted headlines. Not 'it is widely assumed'.

carried_by.by: a model's reading (claude-sonnet-4-6, web search), verified by code: the page was fetched with the honest client and contains the belief's key words

what_the_sources_show.statement: The held sources state with high confidence that CDR cannot substitute for deep emissions reductions but would be needed to counterbalance hard-to-abate residual emissions from sectors like agriculture, aviation and industry, while direct air capture remains essentially undeployed and costly.
what_the_sources_show.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code

direction._note: CORRECTS, CONFIRMS or NARROWS. This field exists so the contrarianism guard can count. A publication whose answer is always CORRECTS is performing scepticism rather than assessing evidence, and is not to be trusted.
direction.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code
direction.why: The passages match the belief's core claims: CDR is complementary rather than a substitute, it is used mainly to offset residual emissions from named hard-to-abate sectors, and novel methods are barely deployed. The one nuance is that S002 also assigns CDR a near-term role in further reducing net em

reader_with_a_decision: A policymaker or corporate sustainability lead setting a net-zero target, who must decide how much of that target to rely on carbon removal (and how much to fund or buy it now) versus how deeply to cut their own emissions. A secondary reader is a citizen or investor judging whether net-zero pledges that lean on removal are credible.

public_record_check._note: NOT 'has anybody published this'. On any contested question, somebody has. The question is whether it has been carried WHERE THIS READER WOULD FIND IT. Run the counterexample hunter on the belief statement, not on the finding.
public_record_check.carried_in_general_coverage: Yes: Land and Climate Review (https://landclimate.org/carbon-removal-must-not-overshadow-decarbonisation-efforts/), fetched 2026-11-27, sha256 709c8d76d638be2c; the page contains 24 of the belief's 40 key words. A model's reading (web search), checked by code.
public_record_check.our_contribution: translation, extension, or correction of the prior art -- say which

kill_condition: The primary assessments and inventories (e.g. IPCC AR6 WGIII, national greenhouse-gas inventories, dedicated carbon-removal stocktakes) all confirm the belief as stated. That would mean: current removal is overwhelmingly conventional land-based (forestry) and novel methods are a negligible fraction. Net-zero pathways use removal mainly to balance hard-to-abate residual emissions rather than to substitute for near-term cuts. The scaled-up removal volumes these pathways assume for mid-century are judged achievable only with large, uncertain growth. If there is no material gap, overstatement or understatement between the sources and that belief, there is no story.

kill_condition_tested.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code
kill_condition_tested.note: No material gap is shown. Novel removal is negligible and costly (S005), countries plan land-based rather than novel scale-up (S003), and mid-century volumes require sustained growth from near zero (S004). The passages do not quantify the forestry share of current removal, and S005 notes DACCS costs

scope._note: What the answer will and will not cover, written at step 1 BEFORE any source is opened, so scope cannot be fitted to the findings afterwards. An omission ruled OUT_OF_SCOPE, and a headline conclusion declared out of scope, must name the question's words or one of these entries (fix 2, docs/whu-fix2-omission-rulings-design.md section 2.4).
scope.covers: The role of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) in reaching net-zero CO2 and net-zero greenhouse gases, both now and through roughly 2050–2100. This includes how much is removed today and by which methods (afforestation/reforestation, soil carbon, BECCS, direct air capture with storage, enhanced weathering, biochar, ocean-based approaches). It covers how much removal modelled net-zero and 1.5°C/2°C pathways require and for what purposes (counterbalancing residual emissions, achieving net-negative emissions after overshoot), and the stated constraints on scaling: cost, land, energy, storage permanence and monitoring.

out.what: Whether specific companies' carbon offsets or credits are genuine or overclaimed
out.why: That is a question about particular market products and verification practices, not about the system-level role of removal in net-zero pathways.

out.what: Solar radiation management and other geoengineering that doesn't remove CO2
out.why: It addresses temperature, not atmospheric CO2 or net-zero accounting, so it is a different intervention with different evidence.

out.what: Point-source carbon capture on fossil fuel plants or industry (CCS without removal)
out.why: It reduces new emissions rather than removing CO2 already in the air. Conflating the two is a common error, but its merits are a separate question.

out.what: Whether any particular country or company is on track for its net-zero target
out.why: That requires tracking specific emissions trajectories and policies, beyond the general role of removal.

out.what: The best policy instrument to fund removal (subsidies, compliance markets, procurement)
out.why: It is a policy-design question that depends on the answer here but needs its own evidence base.

evidence_standard._note: What kinds of evidence the answer will weigh, written at step 1 BEFORE any source is opened (post-study fix 3, docs/whu-fix3-evidence-standard.md). 'measured': outcomes measured in trials, cohorts, evaluations. 'assessed': expert assessments -- systematic-review conclusions, IPCC confidence-rated statements, guideline recommendations. When they differ, the page states both and drops neither.
evidence_standard.measured: Observed and inventoried quantities. These include current annual CO2 removal by method (land-based vs novel), as estimated in national inventories and stocktakes, and today's global CO2 and greenhouse-gas emissions for comparison. They also include deployed capacity and operating volumes of direct air capture, BECCS and other facilities, reported or contracted costs per tonne, measured storage permanence and reversal rates (e.g. forest fire and loss data), and geological storage capacity estimates from surveys. Note that scenario outputs for future removal needs are model projections, not measurements.
evidence_standard.assessed: Expert-panel judgements with stated confidence or likelihood. Examples are IPCC AR6 statements that CDR is unavoidable to reach net zero (and their confidence levels), assessed ranges of cumulative and annual CDR across pathways limiting warming to 1.5°C or 2°C, and judgements on the feasibility, sustainability and side-effects of scaling each method (land competition, biodiversity, energy demand). Also included are assessments of the risk of relying on future removal in place of near-term emission cuts, plus any other review's graded certainty on removal potentials and costs.
